highlight.html: Subscriber-heavy week — quality concentrated in DecidrOS + AI Roadmap. 301 new contacts, but 276 are newsletter subscribers from a large Offline import; only 25 sit on the qualified track (14 MQL+, 6 SQL+, 1 opp). DecidrOS converted cleanly (9 of 18 ex-sub to MQL+, 3 SQLs); Sugarworks added a single lead. The Facebook "AI Roadmap" demo campaign was the standout again — 5 leads, all 5 qualified (100% MQL), producing all three DecidrOS SQLs (Lou J, Rick Mooney, Jai T). One opportunity (Steve Canning) was sales-created in-CRM.

observations.html: Subscriber-heavy, quality-light week. 301 new contacts but 276 are newsletter subscribers from an Offline import; only 25 on the qualified track (14 MQL+, 6 SQL+, 1 opp). Judge the week on the qualified 25, not the headline 301.
DecidrOS quality held — ~50% MQL+ rate. 9 of 18 ex-subscriber DecidrOS contacts reached MQL+, producing all 3 SQLs. The DecidrOS funnel is small but clean.
"AI Roadmap" FB demo converts at 100% again. 5 leads, all 5 qualified, all 3 DecidrOS SQLs (Lou J, Rick Mooney, Jai T) for $1,639. Highest-intent source and the clearest place to scale.
AI Readiness + Mercha FB campaigns: 49 contacts, 0 MQL. AI Readiness AU (24) and Mercha AU Continued (23) drove volume but nothing qualified — ~$2.7k spend with no MQL. Quality / targeting review.

Paid media pulled back sharply — $8,979 total. Meta $7,883 (88%), LinkedIn $700, Google $397. LinkedIn (was ~$13k/wk) and Google are nearly dark. Blended $90/lead, but with 80% subscribers the cost per qualified lead is far higher.

Sales-created pipeline: 1 opp + 2 SQLs in-CRM. Steve Canning (opp), Matt Carmichael, Neil Durrant — all AU, Unassigned product, entered via CRM rather than marketing. Tagging product / source would sharpen attribution.
Attribution gap: 248 of 301 contacts have no country. Mainly the newsletter import + FB Lead Ads. Capturing country on-form would sharpen geo reporting.
